The process fixture uses a transient WatchdogSec=5 unit rather than exercising the deployed unit files at WatchdogSec=45; systemd-analyze verification does not prove runtime behavior of the exact production units.

Valid 10–15 minute installer protection is covered with an injected clock and stub runner, not a real long-running SSH process under the actual worker binary, admission budget, systemd watchdog, and cancellation stack.
The process fixture exercises SIGSTOP replacement but not SIGTERM shutdown with the 75-second application join, 90-second systemd deadline, and a module that ignores cancellation.

Maximum restart cooldown, malformed-ledger 30-second fail-closed behavior, future-clock capping, and healthy reset after five minutes are not exercised end-to-end under systemd; coverage is primarily unit-level.

Remote unknown-outcome handling is demonstrated for a canceled PostgreSQL sleep, but no equivalent process-level SSH or HTTP mutation fixture verifies checkpoint persistence and absence of replay after forced termination.

The fixture checks role-local restart isolation and fresh replacement heartbeat, but does not query application readiness throughout startup, role failure, stale-heartbeat expiry, and replacement convergence.
limitations: This is a static source review only; tests were not assumed to pass and no runtime artifacts, race reports, systemd fixture result, binary hash, or database acceptance logs were available for validation.

The supplied source does not include every implementation reached by module handlers, BootstrapWorkerBudget, deployment installers, HTTP/SSH clients, or deployment/upgrade scripts, so preservation of all native timeout and pool-usage bounds cannot be independently proven here.

PASS indicates no production-blocking defect was identified in the supplied supervision, restart, ownership, readiness, admission, and systemd wiring; it is not a substitute for the mandatory isolated-binary and retained acceptance gates.
